.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r5/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Delivery profile line 28: shaped 0.6/0.2/0.2 behind two zero-weight gates and a functional floor)
evidence: STRUCTURE. task/tests/scoring.toml: [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; [floors] functional = 0.05. tests/scoring.toml, tests/test.sh and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff -q: same; sha256 scoring.toml 95f70d6e..., test.sh bd682592..., score.py 13de2b38...), so no task-side alteration of reward policy. Gates carry no reward mass: score.py:46 computes weighted = sum over [weights] only; gate keys never enter the sum. Gate zeroing: score.py:41 gates_passed = all(score > 0.0); :42 scored_ran requires gates_passed; :44 scored dims forced to 0.0 when not scored_ran; :48 reward = weighted only if gates_passed and floors_passed else 0.0; :83 returns 1 on gate failure. Scored suite skipped: test.sh runs `run_suite gates 1500`, then score.py; `case 1) exit 0` exits before `run_suite scored 11100`; exit 2 (malformed/missing dimension) -> write_zero_reward. A gates-suite timeout/failure exits with the zero reward written at start (write_zero_reward before trap). test.sh removes $LOG_DIR/scored before gates, so stale scored data cannot leak. Gate criteria are single binary criteria with aggregation = "all_pass" (gates/render/judge.toml:15-20, gates/constraints/judge.toml:39-44), so gate scores are exactly 0 or 1. The constraints gate requires a real server-backed shared write (new job + candidate created via UI by a Recruiter and found by the Observer in an independent empty context; static seed, no-op success, browser-only save, job-only app explicitly fail), so a non-working app is excluded before any shaping. Each scored prompt also restates that gate and zeros its own dimension on failure (functional/prompt.md:13, polish/prompt.md:12, visual/prompt.md:12 'minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero'). LOCAL EXERCISE (offline, scratchpad copy of frozen score.py + scoring.toml, synthetic RewardKit JSON, no Docker): render=0,constraints=1 with stale scored all 1.0 -> exit 1, reward 0.0000, gates_passed 0, weighted 0.0; constraints=0 -> same; gates pass, no scored/reward.json -> exit 0, reward 0.0, floors_passed 0; gates pass, functional=0.05, polish=visual=1 -> reward 0.0 (weighted 0.43 withheld by floor); functional=0.0684, polish=visual=1 -> reward 0.441; all 1 -> 1.0; gate key missing -> exit 2 (test.sh then writes zero). FLOOR ADEQUACY: functional weight total 58.5 over 43 binary criteria (weighted_mean), so the floor needs > 2.925 weight units. The two trivially gate-adjacent criteria hro_job_open (0.5) and hro_add_candidate (0.5) give only 1.0/58.5 = 0.017, below the floor; a gate-passing app must additionally earn e.g. hro_anonymous (1.5) and hro_restart (1.5) to clear it. Polish criteria all require concurrency/live features (live board/thread, failed send, session resume), so a feature-poor app mostly farms only visual (0.2). Workbook internal annotation 'passing only the cheap gates earns little' holds: gates alone earn 0 directly and the floor zeros the reward unless real functional outcomes beyond the gate setup are observed. RUNTIME: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; the in-container test.sh path and a real judge gate failure on a dead app have not been measured, hence risk=true.
counterexample: Tried: (1) Broken app that could pass: a static/seed-copy or browser-only-save app fails the constraints gate (independent-context Observer readback of a newly created job+candidate) -> reward 0 and scored suite never runs; even with stale scored results on disk, score.py ignores them (verified locally). A thin real-backend app that implements only sign-in, job/candidate creation, 401 guards and SQLite persistence could earn ~4/58.5 = 0.068 functional, clear the 0.05 floor and then collect visual (up to 0.2) for a total near 0.2 (0.441 theoretical upper bound only if polish were also perfect, which its live-collaboration criteria make implausible). This is a partially working app, not a non-working one, and the 0.05 floor is the template-controlled value, so it is a Note-level observation, not a task defect. (2) Conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app whose judge run times out in the gates suite gets reward 0 via the zero-reward default; that is evaluator failure, reported as zero by the frozen shared harness, not a task-authored gate defect. No credible failure found for this row.
